mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches the type of hybridisation with the molecular geometry and the number of σ‑bonds formed by the central atom?

options.B: sp2 hybridisation – trigonal planar geometry – 2 σ‑bonds

mcqs.explanation: In sp hybridisation one s and one p orbital combine to give two equivalent hybrid orbitals that lie 180° apart, giving a linear geometry and allowing exactly two σ‑bonds. Option B is wrong because sp2 gives three σ‑bonds in a trigonal planar arrangement. Option C is wrong because sp3 gives four σ‑bonds. Option D mixes sp2 with linear geometry, which is incorrect.

mcqs.question: In which of the following molecules is the central atom sp hybridised?
mcqs.explanation: BeCl₂ has a linear shape with a bond angle of 180°, indicating sp hybridisation of the Be atom. CO₂ is also linear but the carbon uses sp hybridisation; however the question asks for the central atom, and BeCl₂ is the only option where the central atom is explicitly Be. BF₃ is trigonal planar (sp²) and CH₄ is tetrahedral (sp³).

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes sp hybridisation?

options.A: One s and one p orbital combine to give two equivalent hybrid orbitals oriented 180° apart.
options.B: One s and two p orbitals combine to give three equivalent hybrid orbitals oriented 120° apart.
options.C: One s and three p orbitals combine to give four equivalent hybrid orbitals oriented 109.5° apart.
options.D: Only p orbitals combine, producing two perpendicular π‑bonding orbitals.

mcqs.answer: One s and one p orbital combine to give two equivalent hybrid orbitals oriented 180° apart.
mcqs.explanation: sp hybridisation involves mixing one s and one p orbital, producing two linearly arranged hybrid orbitals (180°). Option B describes sp², Option C describes sp³, and Option D is unrelated to hybridisation.

mcqs.question: What is a characteristic feature of sp² hybridisation?

options.A: Four equivalent hybrid orbitals arranged tetrahedrally.
options.B: Three equivalent hybrid orbitals lying in one plane 120° apart, with one unhybridised p orbital perpendicular to the plane.
options.C: Two equivalent hybrid orbitals oriented linearly, with two unhybridised p orbitals.
options.D: Hybrid orbitals that are not equivalent and have bond angles of 90°.

mcqs.answer: Three equivalent hybrid orbitals lying in one plane 120° apart, with one unhybridised p orbital perpendicular to the plane.
mcqs.explanation: sp² hybridisation mixes one s and two p orbitals, giving three coplanar hybrid orbitals at 120° and leaving one p orbital free for π‑bonding. Option A describes sp³, Option C describes sp, and Option D is incorrect for any standard hybridisation.

mcqs.question: Which definition correctly distinguishes sp³ hybridisation from sp² hybridisation?

options.A: sp³ hybridisation forms three equivalent orbitals at 120°, while sp² forms four at 109.5°.
options.B: sp³ hybridisation mixes one s and three p orbitals to give four equivalent tetrahedral orbitals, whereas sp² mixes one s and two p orbitals to give three planar orbitals.
options.C: sp³ hybridisation involves only p orbitals, producing two linear orbitals.
options.D: sp³ hybridisation results in a linear geometry with two σ‑bonds.

mcqs.answer: sp³ hybridisation mixes one s and three p orbitals to give four equivalent tetrahedral orbitals, whereas sp² mixes one s and two p orbitals to give three planar orbitals.
mcqs.explanation: Option B accurately describes the difference: sp³ gives four tetrahedral hybrids (109.5°), sp² gives three planar hybrids (120°). Option A swaps the geometries, Option C is false, and Option D describes sp hybridisation.

mcqs.question: A molecule is found to have bond angles of approximately 109.5°. Which hybridisation is most likely present at the central atom?
mcqs.explanation: Bond angles near 109.5° correspond to a tetrahedral arrangement, which arises from sp³ hybridisation (four equivalent orbitals). sp gives 180°, sp² gives 120°, and d²sp³ is used for expanded octet geometries, not 109.5°.

mcqs.question: What is the hybridisation of the carbon atoms in ethene (C₂H₄)?
mcqs.explanation: Each carbon in ethene forms three σ‑bonds (two C–H and one C–C) and one π‑bond. This requires three sp² hybrid orbitals for σ‑bonding and one unhybridised p orbital for the π‑bond, so the carbon atoms are sp² hybridised. sp would give only two σ‑bonds, sp³ would give four σ‑bonds, and sp³d is not relevant for carbon.

mcqs.question: A central atom X forms two σ‑bonds and retains two lone pairs, giving a linear molecular shape (e.g., XeF₂). What is the hybridisation of atom X?
mcqs.explanation: Linear geometry with two bonding domains and two lone pairs indicates that the central atom uses two sp hybrid orbitals for the σ‑bonds; the remaining two p orbitals accommodate the lone pairs. Hence the hybridisation is sp. sp³ would give tetrahedral geometry, sp² trigonal planar, and sp³d would give trigonal bipyramidal.
